definition: Halupedia is an AI-generated online encyclopedia, made entirely of AI hallucinations, by Bartłomiej Strama, a student at Zespół Szkół Elektryczno-Mechanicznych, and Tomasz Mamala.
details: The project began as a method to pollute AI training data. Halupedia articles are generated by a technology called a "large language model" on the AI aggerator OpenRouter. "Every link leads to an entry that does not exist yet — until you click it" While article content is generated, page titles are generated by users. Some users have managed to create articles with offensive names. Many popular pages have political overtones or reference Internet memes. The website has been described as "a snake eating its own tail" and an example of the dead Internet theory.

explainer.lead: Halupedia is an online encyclopedia whose articles are generated on demand by a large language model and deliberately consist of AI hallucinations. Created by Bartłomiej Strama and Tomasz Mamala, it turns browsing into an endless chain of invented pages while highlighting how generated material can feed back into AI training data.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a library where you can write any title on a blank book, and a robot instantly fills it with a made-up story. Halupedia works like that: visitors supply titles, and the computer invents the articles, including pages reached by clicking links that do not exist yet. It can be amusing or strange, but it is not a place to look for trustworthy facts.
tiers.practitioner: The system combines user-supplied titles with article generation by a large language model accessed through the OpenRouter aggregator, creating missing entries when their links are clicked. Engineers examining it should treat the corpus as intentionally unreliable generated text rather than reference material. Other pitfalls include unmoderated or offensive titles and the risk of generated pages being reused as training data.
tiers.paperLevel: Halupedia can be described as E = {G(t) : t in T}, where T contains user-generated page titles and G is text generation by a large language model through OpenRouter; clicking a nonexistent entry invokes generation of that entry. The project began as a method of polluting AI training data and offers no factual-accuracy guarantee. Its known failure modes include hallucinated content, offensive user-supplied titles, and feedback between generated web material and later AI systems.

explainer.example: A visitor clicks a link titled “The Great Tea-Cup Election.” No such entry exists, so Halupedia generates an article for that title; the visitor can then follow its links to trigger still more invented pages.

explainer.intuition: It is an encyclopedia built as a self-growing fiction machine: every missing page is an invitation to generate another one. The visitor supplies the prompts indirectly through titles, while the model supplies the invented substance.
howItWorks: A user supplies a page title or clicks a link to an entry that does not yet exist.
The title is passed to a large language model through OpenRouter.
The model generates the article, whose content is intentionally treated as hallucination rather than verified fact.
The new page joins the encyclopedia, and its links can lead to further entries generated on demand.
explainer.whyItMatters: Halupedia makes the problem of AI-generated text becoming input for later AI systems unusually visible, which is why it has been described as “a snake eating its own tail.” It also serves as an example associated with the dead Internet theory, where much online material is machine-generated rather than human-written.
misconceptions: It is not a conventional encyclopedia with fact-checked articles; its content is intentionally hallucinated.
Users generate page titles, not the article bodies, which are produced by the model.
The whole encyclopedia is not written in advance; missing entries are created when visitors reach them.
